headline: Terminal-Bench audit shows why an all-fail score does not certify task hardness
summary: A September 2026 paper audits the frozen Terminal-Bench 3 / Frontier-Bench 0.1 production record to ask what an all-fail score actually supports. It covers 1,081 pull requests, 639 scored tasks and 28,801 trials. Of 125 tasks with no honest pass, an ordered screen retains 78 as certified-unsolved candidates; the other 47 are broken-oracle, infrastructure-limited, exploit-only-passable or unresolved cases. The paper defines certified-unsolved narrowly: a reference route passed, infrastructure did not dominate, no strict verifier bypass was observed, and all evaluated agents failed in the frozen setup. This is not proof of intrinsic hardness or failure at the intended capability. The task-level audit and token-cost analysis are author-reported and have not been independently reproduced here.
